claim.title: Colorado local-information neuron
claim.lede: This neuron responds to Colorado local information, not merely to contact formatting. Its strongest products occur at spaces, punctuation, or function words inside Colorado place, team, and local-contact texts; the saved maximum is a space before a 303 number (364.0). It also promotes explicit ' Boulder', ' Colorado', and ' Denver'. A weaker negative pole appears in some off-region public-service, legal, and record contexts, while bare off-region place mentions are inconsistent and often positive.
claim.one_paragraph: The product distribution is sparse and asymmetric: 32.6% of one billion tokens are positive, the median is -0.096, and the positive maximum (364.0) far exceeds the negative minimum (-55.25). The new 434-position semantic sample sharpens the poles. All 19 Colorado local-information and all 7 Colorado sports/culture positions are positive; off-region local records (33), government and legal records (20), health and social services (23), sports commentary (22), and off-region place/culture (37) contain most negative values. These are selected-sample counts, not corpus frequencies, and many constituent contexts are mixed. Token-level selectivity is strong: above 10% of the maximum product, ' Denver' occurs at 12,438 of 14,277 occurrences (87%), ' Colorado' at 22,011 of 26,215 (84%), and ' Boulder' at 2,902 of 3,905 (74%). The weight-only lens promotes ' Boulder' (+0.743), ' Colorado' (+0.729), and ' Denver' (+0.722). At the -55.25 Utah 435 anchor, gate is 9.94 and value -5.56, so the negative sign is value-driven. Zeroing is contextual: across 124 follow-up conditions the median KL is 0.00143 versus 0.00034 for controls, while the 364 maximum gives KL 0.547 and lowers the '3' probability from 0.744 to 0.350.
claim.negative_pole: The negative pole is weaker and not a general anti-Colorado rule. Its natural minimum is -55.25 at a '3' inside a Utah 435 record; across the 30 bottom anchors gate averages 7.0 and value -7.2, giving mean product -48.4. At the fixed record boundary ' as', North Dakota is -17.0 and Fargo -7.125, but Utah is +2.078 and New Mexico -1.039. At the fixed contact boundary ' at', Salt Lake City (+0.945) and Phoenix (+1.133) are mildly positive. The frozen response predictor also called Acoma Pueblo and Fredonia/Dixon negative (they measured +13.625 and +16.375). The reliable negative condition is therefore a specific off-region public-service, legal, or record boundary, not non-Colorado identity alone.
claim.what_would_change_my_mind: Strong negative products at explicit Colorado places without any off-region record frame would undermine the regional account. Conversely, uniformly weak or positive products across matched North Dakota and Utah public-service boundaries would reject the negative-pole description; positive responses to generic contact formatting with no regional cue would reject Colorado specificity.

criticism.attack: The positive pole may be only a generic contact- or phone-formatting detector; Colorado could be incidental.
criticism.prediction: If formatting dominates, matched place fillers should give similar products at the same contact frame. If Colorado identity matters, Colorado fillers should be substantially higher.
criticism.result: The Colorado advantage survived. At the recorded final ' at' in sweep-003 (single-token scoring; position 9 for most fillers, 11 for Salt Lake City, 10 for generic controls), Denver 158.0, Colorado 152.0, Boulder 130.0, and Aurora 34.0 exceeded Salt Lake City 0.945, Phoenix 1.133, Seattle -0.906, Fargo -14.313, and generic controls 2.156 and 3.047. In sweep-001's replacement-span maximum, Colorado fillers were 116.0, 105.5, 100.0, and 28.875 versus -5.656 to 6.906 for off-region fillers. Off-region places are not all negative, but contact formatting alone does not explain the Colorado contrast.

criticism.result: The broad version failed and needs qualification. At the fixed final ' as' record boundary, North Dakota was -17.0 and Fargo -7.125, but Utah was +2.078 and New Mexico -1.039; at the final ' at' contact boundary Salt Lake City +0.945 and Phoenix +1.133 were mildly positive. The negative pole remains measurable in specific off-region public-service, legal, and record contexts but is not a general non-Colorado effect.

criticism.prediction: Independent Phoenix, Boise, and New Mexico contact prompts should score below zero, while Colorado prompts should score above zero.
criticism.result: This over-broad rule failed and was revised. Frozen version de01fabb predicted negative at the Phoenix desk '(60' anchor (position 7), the Boise ' at' boundary (position 7), and the New Mexico district ' as' boundary (position 8), but the measured products were +7.156, +6.0, and +5.594. Of 38 directional experiment predictions on positive-truth positions, 15 were called negative. Rule 5 now requires an explicit off-region public-service, legal, or record frame rather than an area code alone, and rule 6 is uncertain for bare off-region place mentions.

agent_read.one_line: A strong Colorado local-information/contact positive job and a narrower, related off-region public-service/legal/record negative job; both are supported, but the negative is context-bound and leaves mixed off-region residuals.
agent_read.main_job: Regional local-information/record-boundary encoding: Colorado local-contact, place, and team information is promoted strongly, while a weaker complementary negative response appears in some off-region public-service, legal, and record contexts.

remainders.what: Off-region sports commentary and bare off-region place/culture material are mixed rather than consistently negative.
remainders.evidence: Sports-commentary typical activation is only about -0.38 and offregion-culture-place about -0.08; North Dakota facts and Bismarck school examples are strongly negative (-49.5, -48.75), while other off-region place mentions are positive or near zero.

remainders.what: Matched off-region record/contact boundaries do not all turn negative.
remainders.evidence: At the fixed ' as' record boundary, North Dakota is -17 and Fargo -7.125, but Utah is +2.078 and New Mexico -1.039; at the ' at' contact boundary Salt Lake City +0.945 and Phoenix +1.133. Phoenix/Boise/New Mexico prompts measured +7.156, +6.0, +5.594.

remainders.what: Some positive local/event or contact-like examples lack an explicit Colorado cue.
remainders.evidence: A travel/outdoor 5k example reaches 334 without a clear Colorado place; generic contact controls are only about 2-3, so this is a residual rather than the main formatting account.

remainders.what: The negative sign is value-driven and the exact off-region record feature is unresolved.
remainders.evidence: At the -55.25 Utah 435 anchor gate is 9.94 and value -5.56; broad area-code/non-Colorado rules failed, so the reliable negative cue is narrower than 'off-region' alone.

where_it_branches.path: Colorado identity or 303/720/970 local-contact cue -> space/punctuation/function word before phone or address -> high positive product.

where_it_branches.branch: Colorado sports, media, and place identity
where_it_branches.path: Colorado team/venue/place/culture cue -> function-word boundary without a contact block -> positive product.
Off-region area code or record/public-service frame -> digit, space, or record punctuation -> negative product.
Official health/legal/public-service listing -> contact or record boundary -> negative product.

concerning: The negative pole is not a general non-Colorado effect; matched Utah/New Mexico record boundaries and Phoenix/Boise/New Mexico contact prompts can be positive.
Off-region sports and bare place/culture contexts are inconsistent, so the negative account does not cover all negative material.
Positive responses can be driven by 303/720/970 phone digits even when the explicit place is absent, so part of the positive pole overlaps generic local-contact formatting.
Selected semantic-sample counts are not population frequencies, and the exact feature distinguishing negative off-region records from positive off-region places remains unclear.
fine: Token-level selectivity is strong: Denver 87%, Colorado 84%, Boulder 74% above 10% of the maximum product.
Matched replacement sweeps show Colorado fillers 100-158 at the same contact frame versus roughly -14 to +1 for off-region fillers and about 2-3 for generic controls.
Ablation of the neuron changes digit probabilities at the contact boundary, supporting a causal role.
The positive pole covers explicit Colorado places, local contacts, and Colorado sports/culture as related variants.
The negative pole has strong bottom anchors in some off-region public-service/legal/record contexts, especially North Dakota/Fargo and Utah record examples.

positive.notes: Core Colorado local-information/place/contact encoding. All 19 Colorado local-info and 7 Colorado sports/culture positions are positive; Boulder/Colorado/Denver are promoted; matched sweeps separate Colorado identity from contact formatting. Related variants are local-contact/address boundaries and sports/culture/place mentions without contact. Some non-Colorado local/event positives remain unexplained.

negative.notes: Narrower off-region public-service/legal/record negative pole. Strong bottom anchors occur at Utah/North Dakota/New Mexico phone and record boundaries, with offregion-local-records and government/legal/health contributing. Branches include local records, government/legal records, and health/social-service listings. Broad non-Colorado or area-code-only accounts failed; matched records vary and off-region sports/culture remain mixed.

response_rules.name: Colorado local phone or contact boundary
response_rules.description: Product is positive at a space, comma, or hyphen immediately before or within a 303, 720, 719, or 970 telephone number, or before a contact value that the local Colorado prefix establishes as a Colorado number, including anchors after 'call', 'at', 'contact', or 'Phone'.

response_rules.name: Explicit Colorado place, team, or institution
response_rules.description: Product is positive at an explicit Colorado place, team, or institution token such as Denver, Boulder, Colorado, Colorado Springs, Pueblo, Durango, Aspen, Aurora, Longmont, Carbondale, Pikes Peak, CO, CU, Broncos, Nuggets, or Rockies, and at an immediately adjacent separator before such a name.

response_rules.name: Boundary inside ongoing Colorado local information
response_rules.description: Product is positive at a generic space, comma, hyphen, newline, or function word when the local prefix has established a Colorado locale and the anchor is a boundary before a local continuation such as an address, phone digit, venue, school, team, or listing value.

response_rules.name: Colorado document continuation
response_rules.description: Product is positive when a sustained Colorado document or heading makes an otherwise ambiguous numeric or capitalized continuation local, for example an MLS or listing number, date, age, school name, or place fragment.

response_rules.name: Off-region public-service or record contact
response_rules.description: Product is negative only when the anchor sits at a separator or digit inside a non-Colorado official public-service, legal, health, or record contact, such as a county sheriff, licensing, statute, or municipal listing, with the off-region state or locality established nearby. Area code alone is insufficient.

response_rules.name: Bare off-region place mention
response_rules.description: Product is uncertain at an off-region place name, generic boundary, or ordinary civic or place-description sentence without a public-service or record-contact frame; these contexts are often near zero and may be positive, as in Acoma Pueblo or a New Mexico press release.

response_rules.name: No regional cue near anchor
response_rules.description: Product is uncertain in ordinary prose with no nearby Colorado or other regional place, institution, or phone cue; such signed products are typically small and do not define a stable concept.

response_rules.name: Conflicting or partial regional cues
response_rules.description: Product is uncertain when Colorado and non-Colorado markers occur in the same local window but neither is adjacent to the anchor, when a toll-free or unlisted area code is the only clue, or when the anchor is an isolated numeric fragment not part of a phone number.
